subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Show that the points in the Argand diagram represented by the complex numbers 2 + 2i, −2 − 2i, −2√3 + 2√3i are the vertices of an equilateral triangle.

mark_split.label: Write the three points and the distance formula
Find the three sides AB, BC, CA
State that the sides are equal and conclude

recall_prompt: Say how you would show that the three points make an equilateral triangle — what you turn each complex number into, what you compute, and what you compare at the end.
insider_note: All three distances are needed — two equal sides only show an isosceles triangle. The last mark is a sentence, not a number: say the three sides are equal and name the triangle.

steps.label: Write the points
steps.margin_note: First mark. A complex number x + iy is the point (x, y) in the Argand plane. Write all three as points and write the distance formula once — every later line uses it.
steps.memory_tip: x + iy is the point (x, y). Read −2√3 + 2√3i as (−2√3, 2√3) — the √3 belongs to both coordinates.

recall.must_convey: That each complex number x + iy is taken as the point (x, y), giving A(2, 2), B(−2, −2), C(−2√3, 2√3), and that side lengths come from the distance formula.
accept: write each complex number as a point x comma y and use the distance formula for the sides
the three numbers become the points two two, minus two minus two and minus two root three comma two root three
take real part as x and imaginary part as y to get three points
prathi complex number ni point ga rasi distance formula use cheyali
convert to points in the argand plane then find the distances

steps.why: The Argand plane turns a complex-number question into a coordinate-geometry question. Once the three numbers are points, a triangle is equilateral exactly when its three sides have the same length — nothing about i is needed after this line.
common_mistakes: Reading −2√3 + 2√3i as the point (−2, 2) by dropping the √3.
Swapping x and y, taking the imaginary part as x.
Never writing the distance formula, then making a sign error inside the root.

steps.label: Sketch the triangle
steps.margin_note: Worth no mark, but it takes ten seconds and it shows the examiner which point is which. The dashed lines are the axes; the triangle sits with A in the first quadrant, B in the third, C in the second.
steps.memory_tip: A in the first quadrant, B in the third, C in the second. The sketch fixes which pairs are sides.

recall.must_convey: That the three points are marked on the Argand plane and joined into triangle ABC. Naming the sketch is full credit — it cannot be spoken.
accept: draw the three points on the argand plane and join them
sketch triangle A B C on the axes
mark A B and C and draw the triangle
moodu points ni plane lo guruthu pettukoni triangle geeyali
plot the points and join them into a triangle

steps.why: The sketch is not proof, but it stops the commonest slip: joining the wrong pairs of points. With A, B, C labelled, the three sides you must compute are AB, BC and CA and nothing else.
common_mistakes: Placing C(−2√3, 2√3) in the wrong quadrant — it is in the second, with a negative x and positive y.
Treating the sketch as the proof and skipping the distances.

steps.label: Find AB, BC, CA
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. AB is quick. BC and CA both have a √3 inside the root; the identity (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) does both in one line each and avoids expanding (2 + 2√3)² by hand.
steps.memory_tip: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) does BC and CA in one line each. All three sides come out √32.

recall.must_convey: That the three distances AB, BC and CA are each computed with the distance formula and each comes to √32.
accept: find A B, B C and C A with the distance formula and each one is root thirty two
compute all three sides and they all come to root thirty two
the three distances are equal, each is root thirty two
moodu sides distance formula tho kanukunte anni root thirty two vasthai
use a plus b squared plus a minus b squared equals two a squared plus b squared to get root thirty two each time

steps.why: Three equal sides is the definition of an equilateral triangle, so all three distances must be shown — two equal sides only prove isosceles. Leaving the answer as √32 (not 4√2) is fine; what matters is that the three roots are the same number.
common_mistakes: Computing only AB and BC and concluding — that shows isosceles, not equilateral.
Writing (−2 − 2√3)² as 4 − 12 instead of expanding it as a square, which is positive.
A sign slip in (x₁ − x₂) when both coordinates are negative.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Say the three sides are equal AND name the shape. A page of correct distances with no sentence at the end loses this mark.
steps.memory_tip: Equilateral needs all three sides shown; two equal sides is only isosceles. Name the shape in the last line.

lines.text: ∴ A, B, C form an equilateral triangle.

recall.must_convey: That since AB = BC = CA, the three points are the vertices of an equilateral triangle.
accept: all three sides are equal so the triangle is equilateral
A B equals B C equals C A therefore A B C is an equilateral triangle
since the three sides are the same length it is equilateral
moodu sides equal kabatti equilateral triangle
equal sides means equilateral

steps.why: The question says 'show that', so the last line must say what has been shown. The examiner marks the statement, not the feeling that the work is done.
common_mistakes: Ending on the third distance with no conclusion.
Writing 'hence proved' without naming which sides are equal.
